title: Pearls and bony-fish otoliths share the structure of artificial calcospherites

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Pearls and bony-fish otoliths share the structure of artificial calcospherites

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The concentrically zoned, radiate structure of pearls and of the otoliths of molluscs and bony fishes is essentially the same as that of the calcospherites formed artificially when calcium carbonate is precipitated in albumin, implying the same physico-chemical mode of formation.

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Ch. IX: On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The typical structure of a calcospherite is no other than that of a pearl, nor does it differ essentially from that of the otolith of a mollusc or of a bony fish.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci On Growth and Form claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: D’Arcy Wentworth Thompson, On Growth and Form (1st ed., Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1917), Chapter IX, “On Concretions, Spicules, and Spicular Skeletons”; topic “Calcospherites and colloid precipitation”. Scope: pearls, molluscan and teleost otoliths, and similar calcareous concretions

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on thompson1917-ch09-04: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.52

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern imaging makes the morphological comparison direct. Data are likely available piecemeal, but the mechanistic inference is underdetermined because similar zoning can arise through distinct matrix-controlled processes.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Quantify radial crystal orientation, concentric zoning, polymorph and organic-matrix distribution in images of pearls, otoliths and albumin-grown calcospherites. Shared multiscale structural signatures would support structural equivalence, but mechanism requires distinguishing common precipitation physics from other biomineralization routes.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Comparable raw images across all three materials are scattered.

Structural similarity alone does not establish identical formation mechanism.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.75
discriminating power: 0.45
data existence: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.35

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The structural comparison is measurable, but the inference from shared structure to a shared physico-chemical mode is one interpretation among others. Otolith outlines are well archived, while matched sections of pearls, otoliths and laboratory calcospherites are not. A subset comparison is feasible from images and scans; it would not cleanly exclude other ways of building the same fabric.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare sectioned pearls, molluscan and teleost otoliths, and albumin-precipitated calcospherites for concentric zoning and radial fabric. A shared geometry supports a common precipitation mode; systematic differences in zoning or crystal habit refute the identification.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Pearls and artificial calcospherites are mostly illustrated in papers, not in the otolith catalogues.

Similar concentric-radiate structure can arise from more than one precipitation chemistry.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
